Retrospective case series of 11 children; only Table 2 rows carry individual data. Most Results paragraphs are series-level and are not copied to patients unless the sentence explicitly covers all patients or all patients of a subtype.
Series-level negatives ("None of the patients ...") are copied to all 11 patients because the sentences explicitly cover all patients.

Source conflict: the text says five patients (45.4%) had possible minor adverse events, while Table 2 lists adverse effects for only three rows (6, 8 and 9); blank table cells are not recorded as absence.

Source conflict: Table 1 gives macrophage activation syndrome at onset in 3 patients (27.2%), while the Results text says two patients had three episodes before tocilizumab; neither is assigned to individual patients.

Source conflict: the text counts seven patients with another prior biological agent (four pJIA etanercept plus three sJIA canakinumab, four sJIA only tocilizumab), while Table 2 lists a biologic (Anti-TNF) for patient 7 as well.

Text gives a median tocilizumab duration of 16 months (range 12-28), while Table 2 durations run from 5 to 37 months; the corticosteroid sentences also give eight patients both as having discontinued and as not completely withdrawn. These are series-level and not assigned to patients.

Unlabelled Results statements (TST/IGRA-positive patients treated with isoniazid, anemia counts, concomitant drug use, corticosteroid discontinuation, MAS episodes, seropositive non-responder) cannot be assigned to patients literally; only the non-responder paragraphs are attached to patient 11 as review_only.
Table 2 VAS1/VAS2 do not state which scale or unit they use; Table 2 disease duration has no stated reference point.
Subtype-level tocilizumab dose ranges are series-level and kept as review_only per patient.
The text says one patient had previously used more than two biological agents, but no Table 2 row lists more than one prior biological agent; not assigned to any patient.

Corticosteroid counts are internally inconsistent: Table 2 lists corticosteroids for only three pJIA patients, yet the text says three pJIA patients discontinued corticosteroids and one pJIA patient continued them; concomitant drug use is not assigned to patients.

Use of tocilizumab was discontinued in one patient and three of four pJIA patients achieved remission; the text does not identify these patients, so discontinuation, remission and ACR Pedi responses are not assigned to pJIA patients.

Table 2 adverse effects are recorded as present events (the text says they were observed) but their causal link to tocilizumab is hedged ("possible"), so they are not coded as complications of treatment.

key_findings: Eleven patients are individuated only by Table 2 rows (p1-p7 sJIA, p8-p11 pJIA); roster order and counts match Table 1 (4 male, 7 female; 7 sJIA, 4 pJIA).

Etanercept for p8-p11 accepted: "For four pJIA patients" equals the whole four-patient pJIA group, consistent with Anti-TNF in all four Table 2 rows.
pJIA remission (three of four), the seropositive seven-month non-responder, rituximab switch and post-treatment anemia are not literally attributable; p11 items remain review_only with an ambiguity.
